title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: As part of climate interventions in ‘Le Chéile: Together for an inclusive better world, this project will advocate and support the integration of climate action into citizenship and political participation work. It is a fundamental human right for people living with disabilities to have their voices heard in decisions that affect their wellbeing. Climate change affects all people; therefore, it is imperative that climate actions and policies include everyone. However, without a systemic process in place to ensure the participation of all stakeholders, the appropriate changes desired by people with disabilities may not be considered in the development of policies. This project will advocate for Organisations of People with Disabilities (OPDs) and youth with disabilities to be involved in climate change decision making with Freetown city council and the Environment Protection Agency in Sierra Leone. Mapping will take place of existing stakeholders, programmes and youth initiatives working in climate change. The project will aim to build capacity for youth OPDs and youth with disabilities on climate change and climate resilience, working together with national civil society organisations and UN agencies specialised in climate and environment action.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Increased integration of climate action initiatives, especially on climate adaptation and mitigation, into eye health and citizenship and political participation work in Sierra Leone.. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Adaptation: - The project will advocate for and support the participation of people with disabilities organisations and youth with disabilities' organisations to engage in policy and decision-making processes on climate change ensuring their voices are heard and included at the national and regional level.
